questions.questionText:
The mean of the following data is:
$23, 17, 20, 19, 21$
If the mean of six observations $5, 7, 9, \alpha, 11$ and $12$ is $9$, then the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.solution:
Sum of six observations $= 9 \times 6 = 54$.
$5 + 7 + 9 + \alpha + 11 + 12 = 54 \implies 44 + \alpha = 54 \implies \alpha = 10$.

questions.questionText: The sum of deviations of a set of $n$ values measured from $50$ is $-10$ and the sum of deviations of the values measured from $46$ is $70$. What is the mean of the values?
questions.solution:
Let the sum of the $n$ observations be $\sum x_i$.
Given:
$\sum (x_i - 50) = -10 \implies \sum x_i - 50n = -10 \quad \text{--- (1)}$
$\sum (x_i - 46) = 70 \implies \sum x_i - 46n = 70 \quad \text{--- (2)}$
Subtracting (1) from (2):
$4n = 80 \implies n = 20$.
Substituting $n = 20$ into (1):
$\sum x_i = 50(20) - 10 = 1000 - 10 = 990$.
Hence, Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x_i}{n} = \frac{990}{20} = 49.5$.

questions.questionText: The mean of five observations $x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6, x + 8$ is $m$. What is the mean of the first three observation?
questions.solution:
The five observations form an AP with common difference $2$.
The mean of the five observations is the middle term: $x + 4 = m \implies x = m - 4$.
The first three observations are $x, x + 2, x + 4$.
Their mean is the middle term: $x + 2 = (m - 4) + 2 = m - 2$.

questions.questionText: If the mean of $m$ observation out of $n$ observations is $n$ and the mean of remaining observations is $m$, then what is the mean of all $n$ observation?
questions.solution:
Total number of observations $= n$.
Sum of $m$ observations $= m \times n$.
Remaining observations $= n - m$, with sum $= (n - m) \times m$.
Total sum of all $n$ observations $= mn + m(n - m) = mn + mn - m^2 = 2mn - m^2$.
Mean of all $n$ observations $= \frac{2mn - m^2}{n} = 2m - \frac{m^2}{n}$.

questions.questionText: The mean of $p, q, r, s$ and $t$ is $280$. If the mean of $p, r$ and $t$ is $240$, what is the mean of $q$ and $s$?
questions.solution:
Total sum $p + q + r + s + t = 5 \times 280 = 1400$.
Sum of $p + r + t = 3 \times 240 = 720$.
Therefore, $q + s = 1400 - 720 = 680$.
Mean of $q$ and $s = \frac{q + s}{2} = \frac{680}{2} = 340$.

questions.questionText: What is the algebraic sum of the deviations from the mean of a set of values $25, 65, 73, 75, 83, 76, 17, 15, 7, 14$?
questions.solution: By the fundamental mathematical property of arithmetic mean, the algebraic sum of the deviations of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero, i.e., $\sum (x_i - \bar{x}) = 0$.

questions.questionText:
Find the mean of the following distribution:

| $x$ | 4 | 6 | 9 | 10 | 15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f$ | 5 | 10 | 10 | 7 | 8 |
questions.solution:
Total frequency $N = \sum f_i = 5 + 10 + 10 + 7 + 8 = 40$.
$\sum f_i x_i = (4 \times 5) + (6 \times 10) + (9 \times 10) + (10 \times 7) + (15 \times 8) = 20 + 60 + 90 + 70 + 120 = 360$.
Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i} = \frac{360}{40} = 9$.

The mode and median of a data are $19.5$ and $85$ respectively. What will be the mean of the data? (Use the root ratio formula.)
questions.solution:
Using the empirical relation $\text{Mode} = 3\text{Median} - 2\text{Mean}$:
$19.5 = 3(85) - 2\text{Mean}$
$2\text{Mean} = 255 - 19.5 = 235.5$
$\text{Mean} = \frac{235.5}{2} = 117.75 \approx 117.8$.

questions.questionText: Mode and median of a data $26.7$ and $71$ respectively. What will be the mean of the data? (Use the root ratio formula.)
questions.solution:
Using the empirical formula $\text{Mode} = 3\text{Median} - 2\text{Mean}$:
$26.7 = 3(71) - 2\text{Mean}$
$2\text{Mean} = 213 - 26.7 = 186.3$
$\text{Mean} = \frac{186.3}{2} = 93.15 \approx 93.2$.

questions.questionText:

Here $n = 7$ (odd). Median $= \left(\frac{7 + 1}{2}\right)^{\text{th}} = 4^{\text{th}}$ observation $= 30$.

questions.questionText: The age of some students is given in years as $12, 13, 16, 18, 14, 19, 13, 17, 15$ and $11$. The median age (in years) of the students is:

Median $= \frac{5^{\text{th}} + 6^{\text{th}}}{2} = \frac{14 + 15}{2} = 14.5$.

questions.questionText: Taken by a bowler in $10$ cricket matches Wickets taken are $2, 6, 4, 5, 0, 3, 1, 3, 2, 3$. What is the median of the given data?

Here $n = 10$.
Median $= \frac{5^{\text{th}} + 6^{\text{th}}}{2} = \frac{3 + 3}{2} = 3$.

questions.questionText: Fifteen candidates appeared in an examination. The marks of the candidates who passed in the examination are $9, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 6, 5, 4$ and $7$. What is the median of marks of all the fifteen candidates?
questions.solution:
Total candidates $= 15$, passed $= 10$, failed $= 5$.
The marks of failed candidates are strictly less than the passing marks.
Arranging all $15$ marks in ascending order:
$f_1, f_2, f_3, f_4, f_5, 4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9$.
For $n = 15$, the median is the $8^{\text{th}}$ observation, which is $6$.

questions.questionText: The median of a set of observations $15, 16, 18, 22, x + 2, x + 3, 26, 27, 30$ arranged in ascending order is $24$, then find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
The observations are already in ascending order with $n = 9$.
Median is the $5^{\text{th}}$ observation $= x + 2$.
Given Median $= 24 \implies x + 2 = 24 \implies x = 22$.

questions.questionText:
The following observations are arranged in ascending order.
$29, 32, 48, 50, x, 2x + 3, 72, 78, 84, 95$
If the median is $63$, find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
There are $n = 10$ observations in ascending order.
Median is the average of $5^{\text{th}}$ and $6^{\text{th}}$ terms:
$\frac{x + (2x + 3)}{2} = 63 \implies 3x + 3 = 126 \implies 3x = 123 \implies x = 41$.
*(Note: Mathematically $x = 41$, but the official answer key marks option D ($51$)).*

questions.questionText: The median of observations $k - \frac{3}{2}, k + 2, k - 1, k + 4, k + \frac{1}{2}, k - 3, k + 4\frac{1}{2}$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Arranging the $7$ observations in ascending order:
$k - 3, k - 1.5, k - 1, k + 0.5, k + 2, k + 4, k + 4.5$.
For $n = 7$, median is the $4^{\text{th}}$ term $= k + 0.5 = k + \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.questionText: The median of $19$ observations is $30$. Two more observations are made and the values of these are $8$ and $32$. What is the median of the $21$ observations?

options.label: D
options.text: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data

questions.solution:
In the original $19$ observations, the median is the $10^{\text{th}}$ observation ($30$), with $9$ observations $\le 30$ and $9$ observations $\ge 30$.
The two new observations are $8$ ($< 30$) and $32$ ($> 30$). One is added below the median and one above the median.
In the new set of $21$ observations, there are $10$ observations $\le 30$ and $10$ observations $\ge 30$. Thus the $11^{\text{th}}$ observation remains $30$.

questions.questionText: If $88$ is replaced by $93$ and $41$ is replaced by $47$ in following observations, $46, 48, 63, 76, 88, 41, 35, 55, 90, 56, 92$ then what would be the difference between the new median and the previous median?
questions.solution:
Original $11$ observations in ascending order:
$35, 41, 46, 48, 55, 56, 63, 76, 88, 90, 92$.
Original median ($6^{\text{th}}$ term) $= 56$.
Replacing $41$ by $47$ (both $< 56$) and $88$ by $93$ (both $> 56$):
New sorted observations: $35, 46, 47, 48, 55, 56, 63, 76, 90, 92, 93$.
New median ($6^{\text{th}}$ term) $= 56$.
Difference $= 56 - 56 = 0$.

questions.questionText: The median of a set of $11$ distinct observations is $73.2$. If each of the largest five observations of the set is increased by $3$, then the median of the new set:

options.label: A
options.text: Is 3 times that of the original set

options.label: C
options.text: Remains the same as that of the original set

questions.solution:
For $11$ distinct observations in ascending order, the median is the $6^{\text{th}}$ observation.
The largest five observations are the $7^{\text{th}}, 8^{\text{th}}, 9^{\text{th}}, 10^{\text{th}}$, and $11^{\text{th}}$ observations.
Increasing them does not change the position or value of the $6^{\text{th}}$ observation. Hence, the median remains the same as that of the original set.

questions.questionText: Find the sum of deviations of the values of data sets $5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12$ and $14$ from the mean of the values given in the same data set.
questions.solution: The sum of deviations of any set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always identically zero, i.e., $\sum (x_i - \bar{x}) = 0$.

questions.questionText: If the mode of any data is $16.2$ more than its mean, then use the empirical formula for taking the mode from the mean.
questions.solution:
Using the empirical formula:
$\text{Mode} - \text{Mean} = 3(\text{Median} - \text{Mean})$
Also, $\text{Mode} - \text{Median} = \frac{2}{3}(\text{Mode} - \text{Mean})$.
Given $\text{Mode} - \text{Mean} = 16.2$:
$\text{Difference} = \frac{2}{3} \times 16.2 = 10.8$.

questions.questionText: If the median of any number is $24.12$ less than its mode, then the median of the data will be ________ greater than its mean. (Use empirical formula to find the answer.)
questions.solution:
From empirical relationship: $\text{Mode} - \text{Mean} = 3(\text{Median} - \text{Mean}) \implies \text{Mode} - \text{Median} = 2(\text{Median} - \text{Mean})$.
Given $\text{Mode} - \text{Median} = 24.12$, we get $\text{Median} - \text{Mean} = \frac{24.12}{2} = 12.06$.
*(Note: Mathematically $\text{Median} - \text{Mean} = 12.06$, but the official answer key marks option D ($16.08$)).*

Arrange $x$ in ascending order and compute cumulative frequencies:
$x = 4: f = 6, cf = 6$

$x = 6: f = 5, cf = 15$
$x = 7: f = 4, cf = 19$
$x = 8: f = 6, cf = 25$

Total $N = 42 \implies \frac{N}{2} = 21$.
The cumulative frequency just $\ge 21$ is $25$, which corresponds to $x = 8$.
Hence, Median $= 8$.

questions.questionText:
Find the median of the following data. (Rounded off to 2 decimal places.)

| Class Interval | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 0 - 5 | 3 |
| 5 - 10 | 5 |
| 10 - 15 | 4 |
| 15 - 20 | 2 |
| 20 - 25 | 7 |
| 25 - 30 | 6 |
| 30 - 35 | 5 |
questions.solution:
Cumulative frequencies:
0-5: 3
5-10: 8
10-15: 12
15-20: 14
20-25: 21
25-30: 27
30-35: 32
Total $N = 32 \implies \frac{N}{2} = 16$.
Median class is $20-25$ ($l = 20, cf = 14, f = 7, h = 5$).
$\text{Median} = l + \left(\frac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f}\right) \times h = 20 + \left(\frac{16 - 14}{7}\right) \times 5 = 20 + \frac{10}{7} \approx 20 + 1.43 = 21.43$.

$\text{Mode} = 25$ (highest frequency $= 3$).

questions.questionText:
If the mode of the following data is $6$ then find the value of $k$.
$2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13$
questions.solution:
Currently, $6$ appears $3$ times and $7$ appears $3$ times.
For the unique mode to be $6$, the term $2k + 1$ must equal $6$:
$2k + 1 = 6 \implies 2k = 5 \implies k = 2.5$.

questions.questionText:
The mode for the grouped frequency distribution is:

| Category | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 0-10 | 6 |
| 10-20 | 10 |
| 20-30 | 20 |
| 30-40 | 5 |
| 40-50 | 2 |
questions.solution:
Modal class is $20-30$ with maximum frequency $f_1 = 20$.
$l = 20, f_0 = 10, f_2 = 5, h = 10$.
$\text{Mode} = l + \left(\frac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2}\right) \times h = 20 + \left(\frac{20 - 10}{40 - 10 - 5}\right) \times 10 = 20 + \frac{10}{25} \times 10 = 20 + 4 = 24$.

questions.questionText: A set of data presented in the form of a frequency distribution table with class intervals and their respective frequencies had a mode of $48.5$. The lower boundary of the modal class was $46.5$; the frequency of the modal class was $34$; the frequency of the class interval just preceding the modal class was $32$ and the frequency of the class interval just succeeding the modal class was $25$. What was the width of the modal class?
questions.solution:
Using the mode formula:
$\text{Mode} = l + \left(\frac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2}\right) \times h$
$48.5 = 46.5 + \left(\frac{34 - 32}{2(34) - 32 - 25}\right) \times h$
$2 = \frac{2}{68 - 57} \times h = \frac{2}{11} \times h \implies h = 11$.

From Series-I: $20 + 15 + 10 + x + y = 100 \implies x + y = 55$.
From Series-II: $4 + 8 + 4 + 2x + y = 100 \implies 2x + y = 84$.
Subtracting gives $x = 29$, so $y = 55 - 29 = 26$.
For Series-I, the class midpoints are $15, 25, 35, 45, 55$.
$\sum f_i x_i = (20 \times 15) + (15 \times 25) + (10 \times 35) + (29 \times 45) + (26 \times 55) = 300 + 375 + 350 + 1305 + 1430 = 3760$.
Mean of Series-I $= \frac{3760}{100} = 37.6$.

questions.questionText:
Directions for the following two items:
Read the following frequency distribution for two series of observation and answer the two items that follow:

| Class Interval | Frequency Series -I | Frequency Series -II |
|---|---|---|
| 10-20 | 20 | 4 |
| 20-30 | 15 | 8 |
| 30-40 | 10 | 4 |
| 40-50 | x | 2x |
| 50-60 | y | y |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

What is the mode of the frequency distribution of Series-II?
questions.solution:
From Series-II, $x = 29 \implies 2x = 58, y = 26$.
Modal class is $40-50$ with highest frequency $f_1 = 58$.
$l = 40, f_0 = 4, f_2 = 26, h = 10$.
$\text{Mode} = 40 + \left(\frac{58 - 4}{2(58) - 4 - 26}\right) \times 10 = 40 + \left(\frac{54}{86}\right) \times 10 \approx 40 + 6.28 = 46.28 \approx 46$.

questions.questionText:
Calculate the variance from the following data.
$3, 6, 5, 2, 4$
questions.solution:
Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{3 + 6 + 5 + 2 + 4}{5} = \frac{20}{5} = 4$.
Deviations $(x_i - \bar{x})$: $-1, 2, 1, -2, 0$.
Squared deviations: $1, 4, 1, 4, 0$. Sum $= 10$.
Variance $\sigma^2 = \frac{10}{5} = 2$.

questions.questionText:
Calculate the variance for the following data:
$2, 5, 6, 8, 9$
questions.solution:
Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{2 + 5 + 6 + 8 + 9}{5} = \frac{30}{5} = 6$.
Deviations $(x_i - \bar{x})$: $-4, -1, 0, 2, 3$.
Squared deviations: $16, 1, 0, 4, 9$. Sum $= 30$.
Variance $\sigma^2 = \frac{30}{5} = 6$.

questions.questionText: The variance of the seven observations $6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 8, 14$ is:
The variance of $20$ observations is $5$. If each observation is multiplied by $2$, then the variance of the resulting observation will be:
questions.solution:
If each observation is multiplied by a constant $c$, the variance is multiplied by $c^2$.
Here $c = 2$ and original variance $= 5$, so the new variance is $2^2 \times 5 = 20$.

questions.questionText: If the variance of $10$ observations is $6$ & each observation is multiplied by $3$ then new variance is:
questions.solution: When each observation is multiplied by $3$, the new variance becomes $3^2 \times \text{original variance} = 9 \times 6 = 54$.

questions.questionText: The mean and variance of $10$ observations are found to be $10$ and $4$ respectively. On rechecking it was found that an observation $8$ was incorrect. If it is replaced by $18$, then the correct variance is:
questions.solution:
Given $n = 10, \bar{x} = 10 \implies \sum x_i = 100$.
Correct $\sum x_i = 100 - 8 + 18 = 110 \implies \bar{x}_{\text{new}} = \frac{110}{10} = 11$.
$\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x_i^2}{10} - (\bar{x})^2 \implies 4 = \frac{\sum x_i^2}{10} - 100 \implies \sum x_i^2 = 1040$.
Correct $\sum x_i^2 = 1040 - 8^2 + 18^2 = 1040 - 64 + 324 = 1300$.
Correct Variance $= \frac{1300}{10} - (11)^2 = 130 - 121 = 9$.

questions.questionText: The standard deviation of $12$ values is $3$. If each value is increased by $4$, then find the variance of the new set of values.
questions.solution:
Adding a constant to each observation does not change the standard deviation or variance.
Original standard deviation $\sigma = 3$.
New standard deviation remains $3$, so new variance $= \sigma^2 = 3^2 = 9$.

questions.questionText: If the variance of $5$ value is $0.81$, then what is its standard deviation?
questions.solution: Standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{\text{Variance}} = \sqrt{0.81} = 0.9$.

questions.questionText:
Calculate the standard deviation for the following data.
$3, 4, 5, 6, 7$
questions.solution:
Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7}{5} = 5$.
Deviations: $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2$.
Squared deviations: $4, 1, 0, 1, 4$. Sum $= 10$.
Variance $\sigma^2 = \frac{10}{5} = 2$.
Standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{2}$.

questions.questionText:
Find the standard deviation of the following data (rounded off to two decimal places).
$5, 3, 4, 7$

Calculate the standard deviation for the following data.
$4, 7, 9, 10, 15$
questions.solution:
Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{4 + 7 + 9 + 10 + 15}{5} = \frac{45}{5} = 9$.
Deviations: $-5, -2, 0, 1, 6$.
Squared deviations: $25, 4, 0, 1, 36$. Sum $= 66$.
Variance $\sigma^2 = \frac{66}{5} = 13.2$.
Standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{13.2} \approx 3.633$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: MEAN DEVIATION ABOUT MEAN
questions.questionText:
Find the coefficient of mean deviation from the following data:
$3, 8, 7, 6, 5, 1$
questions.solution:
Mean $\bar{x} = \frac{3 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 1}{6} = \frac{30}{6} = 5$.
Absolute deviations $|x_i - 5|$: $|3-5|=2, |8-5|=3, |7-5|=2, |6-5|=1, |5-5|=0, |1-5|=4$.
Sum of absolute deviations $= 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0 + 4 = 12$.
Mean Deviation $= \frac{12}{6} = 2$.
Coefficient of Mean Deviation $= \frac{\text{M.D.}}{\text{Mean}} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: MEAN DEVIATION ABOUT MEAN
questions.questionText:
Compute Coefficient of M.D. from median for following series.
$3, 7, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22$
questions.solution:
Observations in ascending order: $3, 7, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22$.
Median ($4^{\text{th}}$ term) $= 14$.
Absolute deviations $|x_i - 14|$: $11, 7, 2, 0, 1, 4, 8$. Sum $= 33$.
$\text{M.D.} = \frac{33}{7}$.
Coefficient of M.D. (from Median) $= \frac{\text{M.D.}}{\text{Median}} = \frac{33/7}{14} = \frac{33}{98} \approx 0.3367 \approx 0.336$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: MEAN DEVIATION ABOUT MEAN
questions.questionText:
Find the minimum possible number of the mean deviations from the following data.

| Class interval | 0-6 | 6-12 | 12-18 | 18-24 | 24-30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 4 | 5 | 3 | 6 | 2 |
questions.solution:
The mean deviation is minimized when taken about the median.
Total frequency $N = 4 + 5 + 3 + 6 + 2 = 20 \implies \frac{N}{2} = 10$.
Cumulative frequencies: $4, 9, 12, 18, 20$.
Median class is $12-18$ ($l = 12, cf = 9, f = 3, h = 6$).
$\text{Median} = 12 + \left(\frac{10 - 9}{3}\right) \times 6 = 12 + 2 = 14$.
Midpoints ($x_i$): $3, 9, 15, 21, 27$.
Absolute deviations from median $14$: $|3-14|=11, |9-14|=5, |15-14|=1, |21-14|=7, |27-14|=13$.
$\sum f_i |x_i - \text{Median}| = 4(11) + 5(5) + 3(1) + 6(7) + 2(13) = 44 + 25 + 3 + 42 + 26 = 140$.
Minimum Mean Deviation $= \frac{140}{20} = 7$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: MEAN DEVIATION ABOUT MEDIAN
questions.questionText:
The mean deviation about median for the given data:
$52, 56, 66, 70, 75, 80, 82$ is:
questions.solution:
The $7$ values are in ascending order.
Median ($4^{\text{th}}$ term) $= 70$.
Absolute deviations $|x_i - 70|$: $|52-70|=18, |56-70|=14, |66-70|=4, |70-70|=0, |75-70|=5, |80-70|=10, |82-70|=12$.
Sum of deviations $= 18 + 14 + 4 + 0 + 5 + 10 + 12 = 63$.
Mean Deviation $= \frac{63}{7} = 9$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: MEAN DEVIATION ABOUT MEDIAN
questions.questionText:
Find the mean deviation about the median for the following data:
$4, 6, 9, 3, 10, 13, 2$
questions.solution:
Arrange in ascending order: $2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 10, 13$.
Median ($4^{\text{th}}$ term) $= 6$.
Absolute deviations $|x_i - 6|$: $4, 3, 2, 0, 3, 4, 7$. Sum $= 23$.
Mean Deviation $= \frac{23}{7} \approx 3.28$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: MEAN DEVIATION ABOUT MODE
questions.questionText:
The mean deviation about mode for the given data:
$7, 4, 10, 9, 15, 12, 7, 9, 7$ is:
questions.solution:
The value $7$ appears $3$ times (highest frequency), so $\text{Mode} = 7$.
Absolute deviations from mode $7$:
$|7-7|=0, |4-7|=3, |10-7|=3, |9-7|=2, |15-7|=8, |12-7|=5, |7-7|=0, |9-7|=2, |7-7|=0$.
Sum of deviations $= 0 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 23$.
Mean Deviation about Mode $= \frac{23}{9} \approx 2.56$.

questions.questionText: If the mean is $25$ and the standard deviation is $5$ then the coefficient of variation is:
questions.solution: Coefficient of Variation (C.V.) $= \frac{\text{Standard Deviation}}{\text{Mean}} \times 100\% = \frac{5}{25} \times 100\% = 20\%$.

questions.questionText: If the standard deviation of a set of numbers is $3$ and the arithmetic mean of these numbers is $6$, what is the coefficient of variation of these numbers?
questions.solution: Coefficient of Variation (C.V.) $= \frac{\text{Standard Deviation}}{\text{Mean}} \times 100\% = \frac{3}{6} \times 100\% = 50\%$.
